chunks: The greatness of God, the Exalted

This world and the next have submitted to Him their reins, and the skies and earths have flung their keys towards Him. The thriving trees bow to Him in the morning and evening, and produce for Him — flaming fire from their branches, and at His command, turn their own feed into ripe fruits.
ai.seo_question: How does Nahj al-Balagha describe the submission of the universe to God?
ai.summary: This passage from Nahj al-Balagha illustrates the concept of *alam al-amr* (the realm of divine command), where creation responds instantly to God's will without intermediary effort. It highlights the Shia theological emphasis on God's absolute sovereignty (*Tawhid*) by personifying nature's obedience, a theme often linked to the Prophet's sermon on the glory of God. The imagery underscores the unity of the physical and spiritual realms in their submission to the Divine.

en.sayed-ali-raza: This world and the next have submitted to Him their reins, and the skies and earths have flung their keys towards Him. The thriving trees bow to Him in the morning and evening, and produce for Him — flaming fire from their branches, and at His command, turn their own feed into ripe fruits.
